mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the tightening signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP signals strengthening economic demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of periods following a 3-month GDP increase, or GDP growth and SPX returns show a negative correlation over a 5-year period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate slower economic growth.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 70% of triggered instances despite the labor market weakening signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production index by more than 2% over two months signals supply-side constraints, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face higher costs and reduced output.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the supply-side constraints signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% and real final sales (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% over two months, it signals robust demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and construction activity boost economic growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% and RSAFS increases > 1% in 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of triggered instances despite the robust demand signal, or the joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS increases on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of periods following a 3-month increase in PAYEMS, or PAYEMS growth and SPX returns show a negative correlation over a 5-year period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 70% of triggered instances despite the inflationary pressure signal, or the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increases on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% and an increase in real final sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% over two months signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and confidence rise.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases > 0.3% and RSAFS increases > 1% in 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of triggered instances despite the strengthening economy signal, or the joint effect of UNRATE decrease and RSAFS increase on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
